title: Public re-exports duplicate between lib.rs and backend.rs; consumers see two paths to the same upstream type
description:
Location: crate-jmap-filenode-server/src/lib.rs:45-49 and
crate-jmap-filenode-server/src/backend.rs:14-17.

```rust
// lib.rs (top level)
pub use backend::{
    AddedItem, BackendChangesError, BackendSetError, ChangesResult, FileNodeBackend, GetObject,
    JmapBackend, JmapObject, QueryChangesResult, QueryObject, QueryResult, SetError, SetErrorType,
    SetObject,
};

// backend.rs (sub-module)
pub use jmap_server::{
    AddedItem, BackendChangesError, BackendSetError, ChangesResult, GetObject, JmapBackend,
    JmapObject, QueryChangesResult, QueryObject, QueryResult, SetError, SetErrorType, SetObject,
};
```

Twelve types (`AddedItem` through `SetObject`) are visible at TWO
paths from the public API surface:

- `jmap_filenode_server::SetError`
- `jmap_filenode_server::backend::SetError`

Both resolve to the same upstream type `jmap_server::SetError`. A
consumer choosing which path to import is making a choice with no
semantic difference but a stylistic one — the kind of choice that
ends up split across a codebase ("I import via `backend::*` so my
trait bounds line up; my colleague imports via the top level so
his match arms line up") and then becomes a recurring nit in code
review.

The duplication is mechanical: lib.rs:45 says `pub use backend::{...}`
to re-export the backend module's types at the top level. That
re-export only works because backend.rs ALSO `pub use jmap_server::*`
those types. The chain is:
`jmap_server::SetError` → re-exported in `backend.rs` → re-exported
in `lib.rs`. Two re-exports for the same type.

A cleaner shape is one of:

1. **Only re-export at the top level.** `lib.rs` says
   `pub use jmap_server::{AddedItem, ...};`. Drop the `pub use
   jmap_server::{...}` block from `backend.rs`. Backend.rs internal
   code can import via its own scope (`use jmap_server::SetError;`
   etc.) without the `pub`.

2. **Only re-export from `backend.rs`.** Drop the `pub use
   backend::{AddedItem, ...}` from `lib.rs`. Consumers always
   reach through `jmap_filenode_server::backend::SetError`.

3. **Drop both and require consumers to depend on jmap-server
   directly for these types.** Most painful for consumers, lowest
   surface area for this crate.

Propagation note: every other extension-server in the workspace
follows the same `pub use backend::{...} + pub use jmap_server::{...}`
pattern. The deduplication should sweep the canonical
jmap-mail-server first then propagate per the canonical-template
rule.

`api-contract,leakage` because two import paths for the same item
is implementation-detail leakage into the public namespace, and
because trimming the duplication reduces the surface area that
must be maintained across upstream revisions.
close_reason: triage 2026-10-22 (already_fixed, skeptic-confirmed): Commit df7d5018 (cites 'JMAP-510h.46 option 1') made the backend module private in every server, so items have one public path at the crate root: crate-jmap-filenode-server/src/lib.rs:35 `mod backend;`, mail lib.rs:48, chat :59, calendars :35, contacts :36, sharing :73, tasks :35. No backend.rs contains `pub use jmap_server`. | check: Every server now declares `mod backend;` (private), and no backend.rs contains any `pub use`. Each item has one public path at the crate root via lib.rs `pub use jmap_server::{...}`, which is the bead's option 1.
